case_name: Smt. Sunita v. Shri Rajinder Kumar — full case name
facts_of_case: The parties were married under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The wife claimed that her husband had deserted her and sought divorce. The trial court allowed the petition.

legal_principles.principle: A petition for divorce under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 is maintainable only if it is proved that the respondent has been guilty of adultery.
legal_principles.held: It is held that a petition for divorce under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 is maintainable only if it is proved that the respondent has been guilty of adultery. The burden lies on the petitioner to prove this fact.
use_in: divorce cases under Hindu Marriage Act

outcome.final_order: The final order was that the appeal was dismissed and the decree of divorce passed by the trial court was confirmed.
